note: Samba 4.17.12 runs its witness service only on a clustered server, so `\pipe\witness` cannot be opened on it and there is nothing to record. This set is derived from two places instead. (a) The DCE/RPC framing values are Samba's own, measured on its srvsvc pipe under the same smb.conf, because [MS-RPCE]'s framing does not depend on which interface is bound: bind_ack is ptype 12 with ack_result 0 and version 5.0, an unknown opnum is a fault (ptype 3) carrying nca_s_op_rng_error 0x1C010002, an unknown pipe name is STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND, IPC$ reports ShareType 2, and a WRITE followed by a READ is an equivalent transport to FSCTL_PIPE_TRANSCEIVE. The measurement is in reference/witness-oracle/. (b) The [MS-SWN] semantics and the NDR encoding of each response stub, checked by handing the stub to Samba's own `ndrdump witness <op> out --validate`, which re-marshals what it parsed and compares: `valid: true` means Samba's NDR implementation accepts the encoding as its own. `witness-register-then-async-notify` is the case that makes the rest of the group mean something: it takes the context handle the service itself issued from a successful Register, and requires that unregistering it succeeds once and then reports WERR_NOT_FOUND. Without it a service that implements only "a handle I never issued is WERR_NOT_FOUND" satisfies every other case, because no case would ever hand it a handle it had issued. Two error codes here are taken from the specification's PROCESSING RULES rather than from the 'most common error codes' tables above them, because the two disagree: 3.1.4.3 lists ERROR_NOT_FOUND in the table and then says a context handle with no matching entry returns ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, while 3.1.4.4 says AsyncNotify with no matching entry returns ERROR_NOT_FOUND. The reference implementation was right and an earlier version of this file was wrong. `witness-register-wrong-netname` exists because the reference implementation had the NetName check switched off so that this probe's own registrations would be accepted; with the check on, a Register naming a different server is ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER per [MS-SWN] 3.1.4.2.
